newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Seeing his national reconciliation move backfiring badly, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh bows to mounting public pressure and promises to revoke his order giving a military pension to former strongman Narong Kittikachorn. Apart from growing resentment within his own New Aspiration Party (NAP) and the nationwide uproar from pro-democracy groups, Chavalit could have been alarmed yesterday by Narong's extremely defiant remark that challenged people opposed to his pension to take to the streets in the hundreds of thousands. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- A special central bank panel has cleared Jaroong Nookwun and two other senior officials from the Bank of Thailand of any wrongdoing in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) fiasco, effectively passing on the burden of proof to the police. A statement issued by the central bank yesterday did not give any details about the investigation, but merely concluded that the three were not involved in any disciplinary violations. (THE NATION)

- Representatives of political parties have offered critiques and suggestions to help ensure cleaner politics and plug loopholes in the current election law. The representatives who attended a meeting organised by the Constitution Drafting Assembly was joined by Constitution Drafting Committee chairman Anand Panyarachun and other CDA members. (BANGKOK POST)

- The cabinet has ordered state agencies to crack down on rampant patent violations to prevent retaliation from major trading partners. The International Economic Policy Committee has told the cabinet that authorities have been ineffectual in suppressing patent violations. (BANGKOK POST)

- The cabinet has settled a controversial Southern Seaboard development project. Proper locations for deep sea ports were discussed and a bigger role for the Southern Seaboard Development Committee was decided. The project was initiated by the Chatichai Choonhavan government, to develop the region as a gateway to East Asia. (THE NATION)
